title: GH#33993: fix: isolate detached headless workers in a systemd user scope
body:
## Summary

Manual-dispatch and CI-repair workers launched with headless-runtime-helper.sh run --detach stayed in the caller's cgroup (plain background subshell), so a KillMode=control-group pulse unit killed them on stop/TimeoutStartSec. _detach_worker now launches under systemd-run --user --scope when _dlw_systemd_user_service_available succeeds (shared probe, AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SYSTEMD_WORKER_SERVICE bypass retained), verifies /proc/<pid>/cgroup names the new scope, and logs worker_detached/worker_detach_unconfirmed. Fallback: setsid when available, plain background otherwise (macOS). Dispatched PID is now the worker process itself.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-tracking.sh, .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — runtime-verified on Ubuntu (systemd 259, OrbStack VM, user manager via linger): production _detach_worker run as the main process of a Type=oneshot KillMode=control-group parent unit, then the unit was stopped. Base main: worker cgroup .../app.slice/aidevops-verify-pulse-base.service, worker KILLED with parent unit (reproduces the issue). This branch: worker cgroup .../app.slice/aidevops-worker-verify-1776-1776-8860.scope, log worker_detached isolation=systemd_scope, Dispatched PID equals worker PID, exported env marker inherited, worker SURVIVED parent unit stop. macOS: test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh 90/90 (production detach + readiness envelope), test-systemd-unit-generation.sh pass, shellcheck -x clean.

## Regression Evidence

The regression needs a live systemd user manager (lingering user session with a D-Bus user bus), a parent `Type=oneshot` `KillMode=control-group` unit, and a unit stop while the detached worker runs; the observable is the worker's `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` and survival. The repository's existing suites run without a user manager (`_dlw_systemd_user_service_available` returns 1 there), and adding a privileged systemd-in-CI harness would be new test infrastructure. Evidence instead:

- Before/after on Ubuntu with systemd 259: base `main` kept the worker in `aidevops-verify-pulse-base.service` and it was killed by the unit stop; this branch moved it to `aidevops-worker-<session>-<pid>-<rand>.scope` and it survived.
- Existing `test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (90/90) exercises the production `_detach_worker` launch, PID contract and readiness envelope on the non-systemd path.
- Production signal: the pulse log now shows `[lifecycle] worker_detached ... isolation=systemd_scope` for each manual or CI-repair detach on systemd hosts; `worker_detach_unconfirmed` flags any launch whose cgroup could not be confirmed.

## Decisions

Used a transient scope instead of a transient service: `systemd-run --user` services start with the user manager's environment and working directory, which would drop the exported worker env contract (attempt ID, git-auth sandbox, PR-repair variables) that `cmd_run` validated before detaching. A scope keeps both, and systemd-run execs the worker, so the scope's process is the real worker. An early worker exit never triggers a second launch; the caller's readiness check reports it with systemd-run errors in the worker log. `KillMode=control-group` on the pulse unit is unchanged.

Resolves #33993

title: GH#33997: fix: refuse checkpoint approval templates that dispatch-approved would reject
body:
## Summary

`approval-template` printed a `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED` line for any release ID. `dispatch-approved` accepts only a trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` from the checkpoint runner closing the named attempt (`pr_checkpoint_events.py` `release_for`/`blocked_release_fields`). Approvals naming `worker_draft_checkpoint`, `crash_during_execution` or `worker_failed` releases could never dispatch. Because any trusted approval comment also disables the legacy continuation path (`pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:141-148`), an invalid approval made recovery worse until someone deleted it.

The template now runs the same `release_for` check against the issue's comments before printing. When dispatch-approved would reject the release, it exits 1 and gives the reason on stderr. `_pcc_approval_template` passes the paginated issue comments to the validator.

## Scope correction (primary dead end moved to a follow-up)

While implementing, I found my approved review's item 1 rested on a false premise. The proactive sweep already refuses to reset an issue that has a closing-linked open PR (`pulse-issue-reconcile-stale.sh:132-145,185-187`), so closing-linked drafts only see the bounded Layer 6 delay. The incident's permanent dead end comes from the pulse's own `checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N` drafts, which reference the issue as non-closing `For #N` by design (`shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:621-629`, GH#32933):

- `_stale_recovery_find_open_pr` uses `closingIssuesReferences`, so the sweep cannot see the draft and resets the issue without a release.
- `_pcc_dispatch` then rejects the draft as unlinked (`pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:70`), even if a stall release existed.

Fixing that makes `For #N` worker-takeover checkpoints eligible for automatic continuation. That is the trust/eligibility policy change the review deferred, so it is filed as a separate worker-ready follow-up. This PR therefore uses `For #33997`.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py` — `template()` validates the release; shared `sorted_comments()`
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` — `_pcc_approval_template` supplies issue comments
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` — template accept/refuse cases

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (approval-chain generator; it can only refuse more, never authorize more)
- **Verification:** `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py` 12/12. The new case checks that a generated line round-trips through `validate()`, and that `worker_draft_checkpoint`, `crash_during_execution`, `worker_failed`, wrong attempt and wrong release ID are refused. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` passes all 56 tests. `shellcheck -x` is clean.

For #33997

body:
## Summary

Resolves #33997. The pulse's own orphan-recovery drafts (checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N, origin:worker-takeover, non-closing For #N body by design per GH#32933) were invisible to stale recovery and rejected by continuation, so a killed worker's issue was reset to status:available and then held forever by worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked. Changes: (1) pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh adds one shared linkage rule (_PR_CHECKPOINT_FOR_LINK_JQ_DEFS / _pr_checkpoint_recovery_draft_links_issue / _pr_checkpoint_pr_links_issue): a PR links issue N via a closing link, or when closingIssuesReferences is empty, the body has an exact For #N line (same regex the signed revision path uses), and it is an open same-repo draft labelled origin:worker-takeover with no origin:worker or protective label. _pr_checkpoint_pr_metadata_is_eligible uses it, so continuation dispatch and the verify-pr-checkpoint-target fence accept the draft; the expected_author check is kept. (2) dispatch-dedup-stale.sh sources the lib, requests body and isCrossRepository in the open-PR scan, and _stale_recovery_linked_pr_rows classifies such a draft as exact, so stale recovery emits STALE_PR_CONTINUATION (draft_checkpoint) and the proactive sweep skips the reset. (3) Already-reset issues: dispatch-stalled accepts, only for these recovery drafts, the killed attempt's own expired DISPATCH_CLAIM/non-terminal DISPATCH_LEASE as stall evidence when it is the newest trusted coordination event and is no newer than the draft head. Any newer claim, lease, release or interactive claim keeps the hold, so it fires at most once per head; the stall-release path and its stalls>=2 attention bound are unchanged. (4) Completion semantics: the continuation worker did not rewrite For #N. The target row now carries a link kind, and For-linked continuations get a prompt step to replace the exact For #N line with Resolves #N and confirm closingIssuesReferences before marking the PR ready.

title: GH#34040: keep worker origin reachable and verify blocked-release commit durability
body:
## Summary

Fixes both defects in #34040.

**Defect 1: the worker network policy sometimes denied the dispatched origin.** Every retained denial was `network.worker-policy` → `git-push-destination-missing` for a bare `git push`. A bare push/fetch/pull resolves its default remote through two git queries with a 5 s hard timeout. Any failed or slow query turned into an anonymous denial. An explicit `git push origin <branch>` was always allowed.

- `command_policy_network.py`: the git queries now get 2 attempts with a configurable timeout (`AIDEVOPS_GIT_POLICY_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 10 s, range 1–60). `_run_git_query_detailed` returns a failure token: `timeout`, `spawn-error` or `exit-N`.
- `command_policy_git.py`: the current branch is read with plumbing (`git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD`) instead of porcelain.
  - If only the branch query fails, the analyzer classifies every remote a default lookup could select (origin plus configured branch/push remotes). Each one still goes through the tier policy. This replaces the denial.
  - A remaining denial names the step that failed, e.g. `git-push-destination-missing(config-query-timeout)`.
- `network-tier-helper.sh`: `check_argv` denials now end with `[layer=… rule=…]` and are written to the denied-access log (`log_policy_denial`), so each denial can be traced to a layer and rule.

**Defect 2: the blocked-release (`permission_required`) path said work was preserved, but unpushed commits were lost.** Cleanup only unregisters the worktree. The exit-time push fallback archived a diff, which is empty for work that is already committed.

- `headless-runtime-failure.sh`:
  - New `_worker_secure_branch_commits` checks whether any commits are unreachable from `origin`. If so, it pushes the branch. If the push fails, it writes a git bundle under the dirty-worktree archive root and checks it with `git bundle verify`. If both fail, it returns `work_lost`.
  - `_push_wip_commits_on_exit` now falls back to the same bundle when its push fails.
- `headless-runtime-worker.sh`: `_hrw_finish_permission_required_run` runs that check and archives uncommitted edits before posting the handoff. On `work_lost` it also writes a blocker-log entry. It passes `--durability` to the helper.
- `worker-permission-helper.sh`: the hard-coded "The worktree and OpenCode session are preserved" line is gone. The comment now shows what the runtime actually verified: pushed, bundled (with a home-normalized path), no unpushed commits, `work_lost`, or "not verified".
